haiku-low.q1: The replica's reports.row_count decides: 10,000 or less streams CSV directly (200 text/csv). More than 10,000 returns 202 and builds in background; user gets status panel and emailed link.
haiku-low.q2: The second click returns the active export (202) with its own filters and columns shown. No new export is created, since one active export per user and report is allowed.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed signed link works 24 hours. The bucket deletes the file 7 days after creation; the page Download works until completed_at plus 7 days, then returns 410.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, with 60 s and 300 s retry gaps. After the third failure the export is marked failed, the upload aborted, and a failure email sent; the page shows Failed with Try again.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica. Export status and writes go to the primary database. Row counts also come from the replica.
haiku-low.q6: Status is stored in the report_exports table in the primary database. The page polls the latest-export endpoint every 5 s while active, and loads it on reopen.
haiku-low.q7: The job streams 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica into a 16 MB part buffer, uploading multipart parts as it goes, so the whole report is never held. Speed under 900 s is not yet measured.
haiku-low.q8: Uploaded parts stay invisible and are aborted by the next attempt via stored upload_id; the next attempt restarts from the first row under a new attempt-numbered key. Nothing is resumed.
haiku-low.q9: The filters and cols text is stored on the report_exports row in the primary database at click time. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job reads filters and cols from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The insert does nothing for the loser, which reads the winning row.
haiku-low.q11: The row must be done, with the file completed and a signed link sent. If rerun while done with email_sent_at empty, the job only re-sends the email. If email_sent_at is set, it returns.
haiku-low.q12: The stream ends early and the page shows Download failed. Try again. Nothing is stored, so the user clicks again. A stream over 10,000 rows is cut off the same way.

sonnet.q1: Step 3 reads reports.row_count (unfiltered total) from the read replica: 10,000 or less takes the sync path, more than 10,000 takes the large path. Sync: 200 text/csv streamed as a file with Content-Disposition, saved by the browser. Large: 202 JSON export state (status panel), and an email with a download link when done.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') makes the insert do nothing. The existing active row is read and returned with 202. The page shows that export's own filters, even if the new click had different filters. If that active row is stale (queued >2h or running >45 min without update), it is first set to failed ('stale'), upload aborted, and a new one is inserted.
sonnet.q3: The emailed signed link works 24 hours (86,400 s). The bucket deletes each object 7 days after creation (a bucket rule set up outside the plan). After the link expires, the user can press Download on the page until completed_at + 7 days; afterwards the endpoint returns 410.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (retry 60 s after attempt 1 fails, 300 s after attempt 2 fails). After the third failure on_final_failure marks the row failed (error_code 'attempts_exhausted'), aborts any upload, and sends the 'report_export_failed' email. The page shows "Failed" with a Try again action, which sends a new request. Exception: if the export was already done and only the email failed, the status stays done and no email arrives.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only (report rows, and row_count too). No fallback to the primary; the job's DB role has no grant on the primary's report_rows. The primary holds only the report_exports records.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row in the primary database (status, attempt, rows_written, etc.). The page loads GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on page load, which returns the caller's most recent export whatever its status. While queued or running it polls every 5 s, stopping at done or failed. A failed poll keeps the last state and retries after 15 s.
sonnet.q7: It streams: keyset pages of 5,000 rows from the replica (about 2-3 MB each) go through the CSV writer into a 16 MB part buffer. Each full buffer is uploaded as a multipart part, and only etags (about 60) are kept in memory. The whole report is never held. Peak memory is one page plus one buffer, well under 512 MB (this is stated but not yet measured; Step 18 checks it). The time target is under 900 s, also not yet measured.
sonnet.q8: Parts stay invisible in storage because nothing appears at the key until complete_multipart. The next attempt aborts the stored upload_id (errors ignored), and the bucket's 24-hour rule discards uploads never completed. Progress is not kept, so the next attempt starts again from the first row. It writes a new file at exports/{export_id}/attempt-{n}.csv. If complete_multipart succeeded but the row update failed, the completed file stays unreferenced until the 7-day rule removes it.
sonnet.q9: The page sends the filters and cols text unchanged in the POST body. They are stored as text in the report_exports row (inserted in the primary). The job payload carries only export_id, and the job reads filters and cols from the row. It re-parses them with the same parser and column check, and nothing parsed is saved.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') in the primary database, plus conditional updates. One insert wins and the other request reads and returns the winning row.
sonnet.q11: Before the email: the row is done (file completed via complete_multipart and the row updated to done with file_key and completed_at) and email_sent_at is empty. The signed URL is created (24 h) and send_email is called; then email_sent_at is set. On a rerun: if done and email_sent_at is empty, it goes straight to Step 13 (sends the email, no rebuild, no permission check). If done and email_sent_at is set, it returns. A rerun may duplicate the email if email_sent_at recording failed (accepted).
sonnet.q12: The stream ends early, with the connection closed without the final chunk. The page's body read fails and shows "Download failed. Try again." Nothing is stored (no export record or file), so the user just clicks again. A database error, timeout or the 10,000-row hard cap (logged) all behave this way.
